question: At what age should an infant start receiving other foods alongside breast milk?

options.A: At three months of age
options.B: At one year of age
options.C: Right after birth
options.D: At the end of the sixth month

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first six months, meaning complementary foods should only start at that point. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h1)

question: A midwife is monitoring a woman whose labor was started with misoprostol. The midwife notices five strong contractions every ten minutes, and the baby's heart rate is dropping. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Give another dose of misoprostol to speed up delivery
options.B: Notify the doctor immediately about uterine hyperstimulation
options.C: Ignore the finding because it is a normal side effect
options.D: Encourage the mother to walk briskly around the ward

explanation: Too many contractions in a short time frame signal hyperstimulation, which can stress the baby and requires prompt medical attention. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why can a shortage of a micronutrient still cause health problems even though it is needed in small amounts?

options.A: They make up the bulk of muscle tissue and physical body weight
options.B: They are the only substances that provide calories for energy
options.C: They act as vital helpers for essential chemical and enzymatic reactions
options.D: The body cannot store any micronutrient for more than one hour

explanation: Even in tiny amounts, micronutrients regulate critical bodily processes without which serious health issues occur. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h4)

question: A patient has a confirmed complete abortion on ultrasound with minimal spotting and stable vital signs. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.A: Perform a repeat manual vacuum aspiration to clean the lining
options.B: Rush the patient to the theater for immediate surgical evacuation
options.C: Provide supportive care, reassurance, and discharge instructions
options.D: Start high-dose intravenous antibiotics and admit for two weeks

explanation: Because the uterus is already empty, surgery is unnecessary, and the patient only needs support and recovery advice. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is a major preventive intervention given to pregnant women during antenatal care to prevent a specific parasitic infection?

options.A: Daily oral iron and calcium infusions
options.B: Routine broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy
options.C: High-dose vitamin A supplementation
options.D: Intermittent preventive treatment for malaria

explanation: Pregnant women receive IPTp during antenatal visits to reduce the severe risks associated with malaria infection during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T2#BMP117_U1_T2_h3)

question: What should a midwife do immediately after applying the ointment to ensure even distribution?

options.A: Gently close the baby's eyelids to help spread the medication
options.B: Cover both eyes tightly with a heavy gauze bandage
options.C: Massage the eyeball firmly in a circular motion
options.D: Flush the eye immediately with warm saline solution

explanation: Closing the eye gently helps distribute the ointment across the surface without damaging the delicate tissue. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h3)

question: A patient cries out with severe burning pain in a foot that was surgically removed yesterday. How should the nurse view this?

options.A: As proof that the incorrect surgical site was operated on
options.B: As evidence that the surgical wound has completely broken open
options.C: As a sign that the patient is experiencing a severe psychiatric delusion
options.D: As genuine neuropathic pain requiring proper evaluation and treatment

explanation: Phantom limb pain is real physical pain driven by the nervous system, and nurses must validate the patient's experience rather than dismiss it. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h4)

question: What does a professional boundary in nursing primarily do?

options.A: Prevents doctors from speaking with midwives
options.B: Ensures patients pay their hospital bills on time
options.C: Keeps the relationship focused strictly on client care
options.D: Stops the nurse from ever talking to patients

explanation: Boundaries ensure that the interaction remains safe, therapeutic, and centered on the patient's healthcare needs. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is it crucial to check and record baseline vital signs immediately before surgery?

options.A: To have a reference point to detect sudden changes during or after the procedure
options.B: To calculate the exact hospital bill for the surgical procedure
options.C: To determine if the patient is well enough to walk home alone
options.D: To prove that the midwife completed their morning administrative duties

explanation: Knowing the patient's normal pre-operative status helps the team quickly spot complications like hemorrhage or shock in theatre. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T1#BMP120_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of the senses is believed to stay active the longest in an unconscious patient?

options.A: Smell
options.B: Sight
options.C: Hearing
options.D: Taste

explanation: The brain's hearing pathways often keep working during unconsciousness, which is why talking gently to the patient matters. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T1#BMP120_U5_T1_h8)

question: What is the very first action a midwife must take when an adverse clinical event happens?

options.A: Notify the family members waiting outside the ward
options.B: Secure patient safety and stabilize clinical condition
options.C: Call the legal department to report the mistake
options.D: Fill out the official hospital incident reporting form

explanation: Preserving life and halting further harm takes absolute precedence over paperwork or administrative tasks during an emergency. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h3)

question: A woman of childbearing age presents with lower abdominal pain and a suspected ovarian cyst. Which test should be performed first to rule out an alternative diagnosis?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy
options.B: Hysterosalpingography
options.C: Computed tomography scan
options.D: Urine pregnancy test

explanation: Ruling out pregnancy is a vital first step because ectopic pregnancies or corpus luteum cysts of pregnancy present with similar clinical signs. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T7#BMP310_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why should you use only the palms of your hands when handling a wet plaster cast?

options.A: To prevent fingertips from making indentations that cause pressure sores
options.B: To keep the plaster powder from sticking to your uniform
options.C: To ensure the inner padding stays completely dry during application
options.D: To make the drying process happen much faster in humid weather

explanation: Fingertips press into soft wet plaster and create dents that push against the skin, leading to painful pressure ulcers underneath. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T3#BMP216_U3_T3_h3)

question: What main event causes heart muscle cells to die during a heart attack?

options.A: Severe swelling of the outer heart lining
options.B: Sudden drop in the total volume of body fluids
options.C: Sudden stoppage of blood flow to the heart muscle
options.D: Rapid increase in the resting heart rate

explanation: Cell death happens because a blocked artery cuts off the oxygen supply that the heart muscle needs to survive. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T4#BMP125_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is proper documentation during the implementation phase legally and clinically essential?

options.A: It provides a clear record that care was safely and timely delivered
options.B: It allows doctors to avoid writing their own progress notes
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between nursing shifts
options.D: It proves to hospital accountants that the patient can be discharged

explanation: Accurate documentation protects both the patient and the midwife by establishing a reliable timeline of care. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T1#BMP120_U1_T1_h5)

question: A maternity ward wants to lower its postpartum hemorrhage rates. What is the best application of quality improvement principles here?

options.A: Banning all high-risk mothers from delivering at the primary healthcare center
options.B: Reviewing birth registers, tracking medication timing, and testing workflow changes using data
options.C: Scolding all midwives during a general meeting for being too slow
options.D: Waiting until the end of the year to see if bleeding rates drop naturally

explanation: True quality improvement relies on systematic data review and testing practical workflow adjustments. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T4#BMP312_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which section occupies the topmost part of the standard WHO partograph sheet?

options.A: Neonatal immunization records
options.B: Postpartum family planning notes
options.C: Maternal blood pressure logs
options.D: Fetal condition monitoring

explanation: The top section of the chart is dedicated to tracking the baby's heart rate, liquor status, and head molding. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which action is a serious ethical and legal violation regarding patient records?

options.A: Writing nursing notes using a black ink ballpoint pen
options.B: Documenting a patient's refusal of prescribed medication
options.C: Adding late entries with the correct current date and time of writing
options.D: Sharing confidential patient diagnosis details with unauthorized visitors

explanation: Nurses have a strict ethical and legal duty to protect patient privacy and must never disclose confidential health information to unauthorized individuals. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T4#BMP110_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why must midwives avoid treating adolescents simply as older children?

options.A: Older children do not experience any physical growth spurts
options.B: Teenagers have completely stopped listening to all adult authority figures
options.C: Teens experience unique biological, psychological, and social changes requiring specialized approaches
options.D: Medical laws prohibit treating teens alongside younger children

explanation: The distinct emotional and physical transition of adolescence requires care that respects their growing independence and specific developmental needs. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T9#BMP126_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of surgical debridement in chronic osteomyelitis?

options.A: To permanently fuse the adjacent joint to stop all movement
options.B: To increase blood pressure throughout the affected extremity
options.C: To replace the entire limb with a synthetic bone structure
options.D: To remove dead bone and infected tissue where antibiotics cannot reach

explanation: Dead bone lacks a blood supply, meaning antibiotics cannot penetrate it. Surgical removal is necessary to clear the infection. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T4#BMP216_U3_T4_h6)

question: What happens to the stored lipids in adipocytes during periods of fasting or starvation?

options.A: They evaporate through the pores of the epidermis
options.B: They transform permanently into water molecules
options.C: They turn directly into rigid bone tissue
options.D: They are broken down to supply metabolic energy

explanation: The body mobilizes stored fat reserves from the hypodermis to provide necessary calories when food intake is insufficient. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T3#BMP111_U4_T3_h3)

question: What anatomical feature forms when the upper uterine segment thickens and the lower segment stretches during obstruction?

options.A: The placental bed
options.B: The cervix
options.C: Braxton Hicks contractions
options.D: Bandl's ring

explanation: Bandl's ring develops as a visible ridge on the abdomen, marking the dangerous boundary between the thickening upper segment and the thinning lower segment. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T3#BMP311_U2_T3_h2)

question: Around which week of pregnancy do the kidneys begin to change?

options.A: Thirty-second week
options.B: Sixteenth week
options.C: Sixth week
options.D: Twenty-fourth week

explanation: Kidney changes start early in the first trimester, around the sixth week of pregnancy, due to hormonal shifts and increased blood volume. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T6#BMP212_U1_T6_h1)

question: During which weeks of pregnancy does a cleft lip or palate usually form?

options.A: Fourth to tenth weeks
options.B: Twentieth to twenty-fourth weeks
options.C: First to third weeks
options.D: Thirtieth to thirty-eighth weeks

explanation: Facial structures develop and join together early in the first trimester, specifically between the fourth and tenth weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T5#BMP220_U2_T5_h1)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for at the beginning of the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Severity
options.B: Situation
options.C: Symptoms
options.D: System

explanation: In the SBAR handover tool, 'S' stands for Situation, which is a clear, concise statement of the current problem. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T1#BMP125_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is it better to use line spacing of 1.15 or 1.5 in professional documents instead of single spacing?

options.A: It is legally mandated for all international health ministries
options.B: It prevents unauthorized persons from printing the document
options.C: It automatically corrects spelling mistakes in the body text
options.D: It gives readers more visual breathing room and space for notes

explanation: Increased line spacing prevents text from looking cramped and makes dense clinical information much easier to read. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which term describes the nervous system control over smooth muscle tissue?

options.A: Cerebellar direct control
options.B: Involuntary control
options.C: Somatic voluntary control
options.D: Conscious motor control

explanation: Smooth muscle functions automatically without conscious thought, making it involuntary. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T2#BMP111_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why should pregnant women avoid contact with people who have active viral rashes?

options.A: Rashes always indicate a severe bacterial infection requiring strong antibiotics
options.B: Viral pathogens can spread easily and potentially harm the developing fetus
options.C: Skin rashes interfere directly with normal maternal blood pressure control
options.D: Pregnant women are immune to all forms of skin-related infections

explanation: Many rash-causing viruses spread easily through close contact and can cross the placenta, leading to potential complications for the baby. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T2#BMP116_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which tool is commonly used to measure changes in knowledge before and after a health education session?

options.A: Pre-test and post-test questionnaires
options.B: National census enumeration maps
options.C: Monthly financial audit sheets
options.D: Surgical theater incident logs

explanation: Administering identical short questions before and after teaching clearly shows what knowledge participants gained. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T1#BMP227_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of amoebic dysentery?

options.A: Bright green vomiting after every meal
options.B: Stools containing blood and mucus
options.C: Complete inability to pass any stool
options.D: Profuse watery diarrhea without mucus

explanation: Tissue destruction in the colon causes bleeding and mucus production, resulting in bloody, mucous-laden stools. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T5#BMP116_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary mode of spreading Staphylococcus within a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Inhalation of respiratory droplets
options.B: Contaminated healthcare worker hands
options.C: Ingestion of unpasteurized milk
options.D: Vector-borne mosquito bites

explanation: Direct hand contact by healthcare personnel is the most common way bacteria transfer between patients in clinical settings. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary benefit of delaying cord clamping for a few minutes after birth?

options.A: It prevents the mother from experiencing severe hemorrhage
options.B: It allows the placenta to expel much faster
options.C: It makes the newborn's skin less slippery to hold
options.D: It improves infant iron stores and reduces anemia

explanation: Waiting to clamp the cord allows extra blood to flow from the placenta to the baby, building up iron reserves for the first months of life. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T3#BMP212_U3_T3_h3)

question: A midwife gives synthetic oxytocin to strengthen weak contractions during labour. Which natural body process is this supporting?

options.A: A positive feedback loop involving cervical stretch and hormone release
options.B: A hypothalamic shutdown of the pituitary gland
options.C: A negative feedback loop that lowers blood pressure
options.D: A steady hormone release that ignores uterine stretching

explanation: Synthetic oxytocin helps the natural positive feedback loop where contractions stretch the cervix, releasing more natural oxytocin. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does reflective listening help during a counseling session with a teenager?

options.A: It forces the client to agree with the prescribed treatment
options.B: It speeds up the consultation so the clinician can leave early
options.C: It proves the midwife is an expert in medical terminology
options.D: It shows the midwife understands and validates their feelings

explanation: Repeating back a summary of what the teenager said builds rapport and ensures both parties are on the same page. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h3)

question: What texture is best for a baby starting solid foods at six months?

options.A: Thick mashes and smooth purees
options.B: Dry biscuits and large chunks of meat
options.C: Whole hard nuts and raw carrots
options.D: Completely watery liquids only

explanation: Thick mashes make it easy to transition from liquids while providing more nutrients than watery porridges. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which emergency makes autocratic coordination especially critical in a delivery suite?

options.A: Conducting health education talks
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Scheduling monthly ward meetings
options.D: Routine antenatal booking

explanation: Rapid blood loss requires immediate, synchronized resuscitation efforts that depend heavily on strict, direct leadership. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T8#BMP312_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the main job of fascicles inside a skeletal muscle?

options.A: They anchor the muscle tendons directly to the bone surface.
options.B: They group individual muscle fibers together within perimysium.
options.C: They store calcium ions needed for muscle shortening.
options.D: They produce ATP molecules for resting muscle tissue.

explanation: Fascicles are bundles of muscle fibers enclosed by the perimysium to help organize the muscle structure. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the correct way to prepare a sputum container before sending it to the lab?

options.A: Leave the lid slightly loose so gases can escape
options.B: Place the open cup inside a paper envelope
options.C: Ensure the lid is tightly sealed and place the container inside a biohazard bag
options.D: Wipe the outside with soapy water and leave it on the tray

explanation: Sealing the container and using a biohazard bag prevents leaks and protects handlers from accidental exposure. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T4#BMP110_U6_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary role of inhibin during male hormonal control?

options.A: Helping sperm swim faster inside the female reproductive tract
options.B: Providing negative feedback to slow down FSH release
options.C: Directly forcing Leydig cells to manufacture testosterone
options.D: Stimulating the hypothalamus to release more GnRH

explanation: Inhibin is released by Sertoli cells to signal the pituitary gland to reduce follicle-stimulating hormone when sperm production is sufficient. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T4#BMP210_U3_T4_h3)

question: What normally protects the stomach lining from its own digestive juices?

options.A: Protective bile salts produced in the gallbladder
options.B: A thick layer of mucus and bicarbonate
options.C: Digestive pepsin enzymes released by the liver
options.D: Strong concentrated layers of hydrochloric acid

explanation: The stomach lining secretes mucus and bicarbonate to form a physical and chemical barrier against harsh acids. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T4#BMP125_U3_T4_h1)

question: Where do secondary bone tumors typically originate?

options.A: From normal calcium deposits during pregnancy
options.B: From cartilage cells inside the knee joint
options.C: From chronic bacterial infections in the marrow
options.D: From primary cancers located in other organs

explanation: Secondary bone tumors are metastatic growths that have traveled from a primary cancer site, such as the breast or lung, to the skeletal system. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the main reason an oropharyngeal airway is placed in an unconscious patient?

options.A: To allow the patient to speak clearly before waking up fully
options.B: To prevent the patient from biting their lip during surgery
options.C: To prevent the tongue from falling backward and blocking the throat
options.D: To deliver high-pressure mechanical ventilation directly to the lungs

explanation: An oropharyngeal airway physically holds the tongue away from the back of the throat to keep the airway open. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T3#BMP120_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why should a midwife assess a patient's learning needs before starting health education?

options.A: To determine the exact financial income of the patient
options.B: To select which doctor will perform the surgery
options.C: To avoid teaching things the patient already knows
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital accreditation paperwork

explanation: Assessment ensures that teaching is targeted, efficient, and directly relevant to the specific gaps in the patient's knowledge. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why are tetracyclines avoided during breastfeeding?

options.A: They change the color of the breast milk
options.B: They dry up all maternal milk production
options.C: The drug passes into breast milk and can affect the infant
options.D: Breast milk breaks down the drug into toxins

explanation: Tetracyclines pass into breast milk, exposing the nursing baby to risks like tooth discoloration and bone growth changes. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T5#BMP124_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of Entonox during childbirth?

options.A: It puts the mother into a deep sleep during delivery
options.B: It leaves the body very quickly once the mask is removed
options.C: It completely blocks all pain in the lower body
options.D: It requires no breathing technique from the woman

explanation: Nitrous oxide is quickly breathed out through the lungs, so its effects wear off almost immediately after stopping inhalation. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h5)

question: In which layer of the skin do you find the secretory coils of sweat glands?

options.A: Basal layer
options.B: Dermis
options.C: Epidermis
options.D: Hypodermis

explanation: Sweat glands are tubular structures with their secretory coils located within the dermal layer of the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T11#BMP111_U4_T11_h1)

question: Where should placentas awaiting delayed disposal be temporarily stored?

options.A: In an open bucket under the delivery bed
options.B: Inside the general staff room kitchenette
options.C: In a dedicated refrigerator separate from food and vaccines
options.D: On top of the clean linen storage trolley

explanation: Temporary cold storage prevents putrefaction, but it must be completely isolated from food or medical vaccines to avoid cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which layer of the skin is the main barrier against drug absorption?

options.A: Basal cell membrane
options.B: Dermal blood vessel
options.C: Stratum corneum
options.D: Subcutaneous layer

explanation: The stratum corneum is the outermost layer made of dead, protective cells. It blocks most foreign substances and chemicals from easily entering the body. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T4#BMP120_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which physical sign on the cervix is commonly seen with a Trichomonas infection?

options.A: Extensive ulcerations resembling herpes lesions
options.B: A smooth, pale cervix with closed os
options.C: Strawberry cervix with punctate hemorrhages
options.D: A thick, white mucous plug blocking the os

explanation: Tiny red spots appear on the cervix due to irritated blood vessels, giving it a look that midwives often describe like a strawberry. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T6#BMP116_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of gastrointestinal absorption?

options.A: To move digested food into the blood or lymph
options.B: To produce digestive enzymes for the stomach
options.C: To eliminate waste products from the body
options.D: To break down large food molecules into smaller pieces

explanation: Absorption is the transfer of processed nutrients from the gut lumen into the circulatory and lymphatic systems for body use. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T3#BMP121_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following devices is NOT used to support body alignment?

options.A: Intravenous infusion pole
options.B: Footboard
options.C: Trochanter roll
options.D: Sandbag

explanation: An intravenous infusion pole is used to hang fluid bags, whereas trochanter rolls, footboards, and sandbags are direct body alignment support devices. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h4)

question: A mother presents on day three after delivery with a fever, lower tummy pain, and foul-smelling lochia. What condition should the midwife suspect first?

options.A: Normal postpartum involution
options.B: Gestational hypertension
options.C: Breast engorgement
options.D: Puerperal endometritis

explanation: Foul-smelling lochia, tender uterus, and fever are classic warning signs of a uterine infection after childbirth. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T6#BMP116_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why must the urinary bladder be emptied immediately before this surgery?

options.A: To allow the baby to turn head-down naturally
options.B: To prevent accidental trauma to the bladder during manipulation
options.C: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: To stimulate stronger uterine contractions

explanation: An overdistended bladder sits higher in the pelvis and is easily injured by instruments or traction during obstructed labor procedures. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T6#BMP311_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for balance and smooth movement?

options.A: The cerebellum
options.B: The pituitary gland
options.C: The cerebrum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: The cerebellum focuses on fine-tuning muscle movements and keeping posture and balance steady during physical activities. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T2#BMP121_U5_T2_h3)

question: A patient managing nephrotic syndrome notices puffiness around their eyes every morning for three days. What should they do first?

options.A: Contact their healthcare provider to report a potential flare-up.
options.B: Double their daily dietary protein intake.
options.C: Stop taking all diuretic medications immediately.
options.D: Exercise vigorously to sweat out the fluid.

explanation: Morning facial puffiness is an early sign that fluid retention is returning and indicates a possible relapse that needs medical attention. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T5#BMP216_U1_T5_h8)

question: What connects skeletal muscles to bones to help create movement?

options.A: Tendons
options.B: Ligaments
options.C: Joint capsules
options.D: Cartilage

explanation: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones so that when muscles pull, the bones move. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T1#BMP111_U2_T1_h3)

question: How do drugs like albendazole and mebendazole kill intestinal worms?

options.A: By cutting off the oxygen supply to the worm's lungs
options.B: By blocking glucose uptake and starving the parasite
options.C: By causing immediate relaxation of all worm muscles
options.D: By dissolving the outer protective skin of the worm

explanation: These medications stop worms from absorbing glucose, which starves them of the energy they need to survive. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T10#BMP124_U4_T10_h3)

question: How does the nursing process help Nigerian midwives manage busy wards with heavy patient loads?

options.A: By enabling systematic prioritization of high-risk patients and efficient resource use
options.B: By eliminating the need to monitor vital signs during active labor
options.C: By transferring all nursing responsibilities to hospital administrators
options.D: By automatically doubling the number of staff available on each shift

explanation: Systematic organization helps clinicians identify critical emergencies quickly even when resources are stretched. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T1#BMP120_U1_T1_h7)

question: What happens to the pelvic organs when the uterosacral and cardinal ligaments lose their strength?

options.A: They rotate 180 degrees inside the peritoneal cavity
options.B: They shift laterally toward the pelvic sidewalls
options.C: They are pulled upward toward the diaphragm
options.D: They descend downward into the vaginal canal

explanation: These specific ligaments anchor the upper vagina and uterus; when they weaken, gravity and abdominal pressure cause the uterus to drop. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which ion rushes into the neuron when an impulse first starts?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Chloride

explanation: When a nerve signal starts, special channels open up and allow sodium ions to rush inside, changing the cell charge from negative to positive. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T5#BMP121_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is a potential risk when using non-selective beta-blockers in patients with breathing problems?

options.A: Rapid expansion of lung capacity
options.B: Relaxation of the airways
options.C: Increased oxygen exchange
options.D: Tightening of the airways

explanation: Non-selective beta-blockers can block beta-2 receptors in the lungs and cause the airways to narrow, which is dangerous for patients with asthma. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T3#BMP124_U2_T3_h4)

question: How might an infant typically react during interactions with a mother experiencing severe, untreated depression?

options.A: Showing reduced eye contact and muted emotional responsiveness
options.B: Sleeping peacefully through the entire day and night without crying
options.C: Exhibiting constant joy and eagerness to explore new surroundings
options.D: Displaying advanced language skills and early independence

explanation: Infants mirror their environment and often become withdrawn, fussy, or unresponsive when their primary caregiver is emotionally detached. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T1#BMP223_U3_T1_h6)

question: How should an examiner generally behave during an active OSCE station?

options.A: Chat warmly with the student to reduce examination anxiety
options.B: Leave the room and grade based on the finished product
options.C: Remain a silent, neutral observer with a blank expression
options.D: Actively guide the student step-by-step through the task

question: What happens to the normal vaginal pH during a Trichomonas vaginalis infection?

question: What happens in a laboratory test when a patient's blood sample is genuinely Rh-positive?

question: Why might a patient withhold important health information due to a psychological barrier?

options.D: They prefer to write everything in a personal diary

question: Which white blood cells arrive first at a wound site during the inflammatory phase?

question: A midwife realizes she forgot to record several medication doses given hours earlier. What should she do?

question: What does the FIFO inventory rule stand for and aim to prevent?

options.A: Found-Item, Filed-Out, used to track broken surgical instruments

options.C: First-In, First-Out, used to prevent medication and consumable expiration
options.D: Fast-In, Final-Out, used to speed up patient discharge procedures

question: What is the main effect of giving opioids to a woman in labour?

options.A: Lowering the mother's blood pressure by constricting major blood vessels

question: What is the main purpose of performing ultrasound scans with Doppler studies in a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic makeup and blood group of the fetus

options.C: To prevent the onset of gestational diabetes mellitus in the mother

question: A postpartum mother complains of numbness and weakness in one leg after a long, difficult labor. What is the most likely cause?

question: A baby is born breathing very slowly thirty minutes after the mother received IV pethidine. What is the immediate priority?

question: Which previous infection is most commonly linked to acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria

question: What does the letter 'O' stand for in the GOBI child survival strategy?

options.A: Oxygen therapy distribution

question: Which mineral is mainly responsible for regulating fluid volume outside of cells?

options.A: Magnesium
options.B: Potassium

question: How can indoor cooking smoke trigger asthma attacks in local communities?

options.A: The heat melts the cartilage inside the windpipe
options.B: They release heavy moisture that floods the lungs with water

options.D: Chemical fumes permanently block oxygen from binding to red blood cells

question: Why is helping a panicked, hyperventilating asthma patient stay calm an important nursing priority?

options.A: Anxiety increases oxygen demand and worsens bronchial muscle constriction

options.C: Fear neutralizes the effect of all emergency inhaler medications

question: In a face presentation, which part of the baby leads the way through the birth canal?

question: A midwife notices that the umbilical cord hanging from the vagina has suddenly grown longer and the uterus is globular. What do these signs tell her?

question: What is the primary cause of a post-dural puncture headache after a spinal block?

options.A: Too much caffeine consumed before coming to the hospital

question: Which laboratory parameter is routinely checked at antenatal clinics to screen for maternal anaemia?

question: How is the sampling interval calculated in systematic sampling?

question: A postpartum mother with a perineal tear has a poor diet lacking protein and vitamin C. How will this affect her healing?

question: Why might some women experience a dry mouth or mild tingling while using Entonox?

options.B: They mean the blood pressure has risen dangerously

question: A woman accidentally steps on a rusty nail at a farm and has not had a tetanus shot in ten years. Which type of artificial protection does she need right away?

options.A: No medical treatment is needed since rusty nails only cause minor skin irritation
options.B: Oral antibiotics only, because bacteria cannot survive in deep muscle tissue
options.C: Passive immunity through tetanus antitoxin or immunoglobulin for immediate defense
options.D: Active immunity through a tetanus vaccine so she can build her own antibodies next month

question: What vital safety check must a midwife do right before injecting bupivacaine into the perineum?

question: Why should calcium supplements be taken at a different time from iron tablets?

question: A midwife notices the deceased person's jaw is dropping open before transfer. What simple action should she take?

question: A patient on tuberculosis treatment reports that their urine has turned bright orange and wants to stop taking the drugs. What is the best nursing response?

question: Which situation requires an emergency vaginal exam during labor?

question: Which of the mother's organs ultimately gets rid of fetal metabolic waste products?

question: Which hormone does the body release during deep sleep to help repair tissues and heal wounds?

question: Why must sebaceous glands continuously produce new cells in their basal layer?

question: Which cells are responsible for remembering a vaccine antigen for a long time?

question: What is the main job of the Peripheral Nervous System in relation to the Central Nervous System?

question: How does a localized wound infection delay the normal healing process?

question: An educator wants to prepare a small group session on postpartum care. What is the most important first step?

question: Why is dense irregular connective tissue well-suited for the deep layer of the skin (dermis)?

question: Why must midwives tell pregnant women never to use over-the-counter diuretics for swollen feet?

question: A midwife finishes conducting a clean vaginal examination on a stable antenatal patient. What should she do next regarding her gloves?

question: What specific bacterial structures do cephalosporins bind to in order to work?

question: When organizing a busy shift, which category of needs must a midwife manage first?

question: What does thick, green, and pus-like sputum usually suggest?

question: Which body fluid is NOT considered potentially infectious under standard precautions?

question: What is the main reason why a pregnant woman's nutritional needs increase?

question: Which of the following is NOT required when documenting end-of-life care?

question: What is the medical term for having an abnormally high volume of amniotic fluid?
